title: Mary-Louise O’Callaghan
gist: Author profile page for Mary-Louise O'Callaghan, a Solomon Islands-based journalist with three decades covering the Pacific, including a Gold Walkley-winning investigation of PNG's use of foreign mercenaries in Bougainville and a stint as RAMSI's public affairs manager.

insights.claim: Mary-Louise O'Callaghan is a journalist and strategic communications specialist with more than three decades' experience in the Pacific, based in Solomon Islands, who reported on political, security and development issues for Australian metropolitan newspapers.
insights.speaker: Lowy Institute — The Interpreter
insights.so_what: Establishes on-the-ground credibility for her Interpreter commentary on Australian policy in Solomon Islands and the wider Pacific.

insights.claim: In 1997 O'Callaghan won the Gold Walkley for exposing the Papua New Guinea Government's decision to hire foreign mercenaries during the Bougainville conflict, later published as the book 'Enemies Within: Australia, PNG and the Sandline Mercenary Affair'.
insights.speaker: Lowy Institute — The Interpreter
insights.so_what: Track record of investigative work on Pacific security crises lends weight to her critiques of Australian Pacific policy.
insights.quote: In 1997, she won the Gold Walkley for her investigation exposing the Papua New Guinea Government’s decision to hire foreign mercenaries during the Bougainville conflict.

insights.claim: O'Callaghan served as Public Affairs Manager for the Regional Assistance Mission to Solomon Islands (RAMSI) and has held senior communications roles at World Vision Australia, Médecins Sans Frontières, Internews and the Asian Development Bank.
insights.speaker: Lowy Institute — The Interpreter
insights.so_what: Insider experience of Australia's flagship Solomons intervention gives context to her assessment of current Australian aid and security spending there.
insights.locator: She subsequently served as Public Affairs

insights.claim: O'Callaghan, now based in Melbourne after teaching investigative journalism at Monash University and working on governance and media development programs in Solomon Islands, continues to write on Pacific affairs for The Interpreter, including on Australia's spending in Solomon Islands.
insights.speaker: Lowy Institute — The Interpreter
insights.so_what: Flags her as a recurring voice critical of Australian aid strategy in the Pacific.
insights.locator: Mary-Louise is currently based in Melbourne
